name: James
bio: James, one of Jesus's brothers along with Joses, Simon, and Judas, is named by the skeptical people of Nazareth who took offense at Jesus's teaching despite knowing his humble family (Matthew 13:55-57). He is a different figure from the apostles James son of Zebedee and James son of Alphaeus; his later leadership of the Jerusalem church and authorship of the Epistle of James are told in the books ahead. When some Judean believers taught that Gentiles must be circumcised to be saved, Paul and Barnabas brought the dispute before the apostles and elders in Jerusalem. After Peter argued that God had already accepted the Gentiles by faith alone, James, as leader of the council, concurred, citing the prophets, and proposed that Gentile believers be asked only to abstain from food polluted by idols, sexual immorality, meat from strangled animals, and blood; his judgment was adopted and sent by letter to the church in Antioch (Acts 15:1-29).
